pairs_touching.what_says_this: Only evidence is CO-OCCURRENCE (2 times in the same contribution's labels[]). a is Williamson's knowledge-account-of-assertion norm (Assertion(p)->Responsibility(p)); b is an anti-luminosity principle (P(x) not=> Accessible(P(x))). Both are plausibly drawn from the same Williamson reading session but no row or lineage_claim connects the two specific principles.
pairs_touching.what_would_make_this_wrong: Would be wrong if a later row explicitly derives the assertion-responsibility norm from the anti-luminosity principle (e.g. 'one cannot always know whether one knows, so assertion responsibility must not presuppose luminous self-knowledge').

pairs_touching.what_says_this: CO-OCCURRENCE (2x), sharing S2528/S2530: both are named sections (EL.2 Epistemic Non-Transparency, EL.3 Knowledge Iteration Non-Closure) of one proposed 8-section theory addition 'EPISTEMIC LIMITS, ACCESSIBILITY AND KNOWLEDGE STANDING'. Sibling-sections-of-one-proposal pattern.
pairs_touching.what_would_make_this_wrong: A row stating the non-transparency principle was derived from, or is a special case of, the iteration-non-closure result (rather than both being independent Williamson-derived sections of the same package).

pairs_touching.notes_for_p3b: Both fully sampled (8 of 8, 4 of 4, no truncation) -- high confidence in the corroborated dual-labeling; the EXTENSION direction (b as instantiation of a's general principle) is INFERRED from Williamson's own external theory structure, flagged for a P3b philosophy-literate check.
pairs_touching.what_says_this: a and b share multiple verbatim-identical dual-labeled rows from the same sources: S2528's 8-section theory-addition list ('EL.1 Factivity...EL.2 Epistemic Non-Transparency [DERIVED]...EL.5 Margin of Error [PROP]...') and its seven-item rejection list, plus S2530's final recommendation table, all appear identically under both families. EL.2 (a's topic) and EL.5 (b's topic) are sibling sub-sections of the same 'EPISTEMIC LIMITS, ACCESSIBILITY AND KNOWLEDGE STANDING' theory addition, both derived from the same S2530 Williamson luminosity/anti-luminosity source material -- in Williamson's own epistemology, margin-for-error is the generating mechanism for anti-luminosity/non-transparency, so b's specific quantitative principle (Known(p)=>Margin(p,Gamma)>0) is a specific instantiation extending a's general principle (P(x) not=> Accessible(P(x))).
pairs_touching.what_would_make_this_wrong: If the corpus treats EL.2 and EL.5 as fully independent derivations from Williamson with no acknowledged conceptual dependency (the shared-document co-listing being purely organizational, not substantive), which would soften this toward UNWITNESSED for the specific EXTENSION direction while the dual-labeling would still support at least SAME-SOURCE-SIBLING framing.

pairs_touching.notes_for_p3b: Same source_id (S2528) producing both families' primary evidence is unusually strong corroboration for a within-one-document EXTENSION.
pairs_touching.what_says_this: Both families derive from the identical source document S2528 (the '8-section theory addition EPISTEMIC LIMITS, ACCESSIBILITY AND KNOWLEDGE STANDING' row appears verbatim in both a_rows_sample and b_rows_sample). a establishes the general non-transparency principle (Eval(P) may be undefined/inaccessible even when P is determinate); b's three-way UNKNOWN classification (Unknown_current, Unknown_access, Unknown_structural) explicitly 'distinguish[es] intrinsic epistemic limits from contingent computational/causal limitations' -- Unknown_access is a direct operational instantiation of a's core non-transparency principle (a property can hold without being accessible), with Unknown_structural and Unknown_current adding further categories not present in a alone.
pairs_touching.what_would_make_this_wrong: If Unknown_access in b were later shown to derive from a different, unrelated non-transparency-like source rather than from S2528's own EL.2 section, this direct link would weaken.

rationale_evidence.anchor: one may not be in a position to know what one's own rational requirements or evidence are. ... Epistemic Property not=> Accessible(Epistemic Property) ... Knowledge(p) not=> Knowledge(Knowledge(p)) ... Eval(P) may be undefined or epistemically inaccessible even when P has a determinate truth value.
rationale_evidence.statement: States epistemic non-transparency as the strongest single Williamson contribution: an epistemic property (knowledge, evidence, rational requirement) can hold without being accessible to the subject/evaluator, giving a formal reason Sat/Eval_c must not be assumed luminous and must not be confused with truth. Status: [DERIVED - very strong].

rationale_evidence.anchor: A condition C is defined to be luminous if and only if: For every case alpha, if in alpha C obtains, then in alpha one is in a position to know that C obtains. ... The Sorites-Style Argument [feeling cold at dawn to hot at noon] ... Therefore the condition 'one feels cold' is not luminous.
rationale_evidence.statement: Gives the formal definition of luminosity (a condition C is luminous iff whenever C obtains one is in a position to know it obtains) and the full sorites-style anti-luminosity argument (feeling-cold-at-dawn-to-hot-at-noon, imperceptible per-step changes) proving virtually no mental state is luminous, including love/hope examples generalizing beyond feeling-cold; grounds the epistemic-non-transparency principle with its original formal source material.

rationale_evidence.anchor: if we combine the argument with the principle that one is always in a position to know what one's evidence is, the upshot is that one has exactly the same evidence in an ordinary case and its sceptical counterpart. ... Luminous conditions are trivial. Since mental states are non-luminous, the sceptical argument fails. ... KnowledgeOS should not adopt a phenomenal conception of evidence.
rationale_evidence.statement: Uses non-luminosity to dissolve philosophical scepticism (if evidence were luminous, evidence would be identical between ordinary and sceptical cases, but mental states are non-luminous so the argument fails) and explicitly rejects the phenomenal conception of evidence (a converging-to-the-empty-set sequence of ever-more-private appearances), translated as: KnowledgeOS's evidence must not be modeled as private/phenomenal appearances.

rationale_evidence.anchor: just as one cannot always know what one's evidence is, so one cannot always know what rationality requires of one. ... rationality is not luminous. ... the system cannot assume that Determination is always accessible.
rationale_evidence.statement: Extends non-luminosity specifically to rationality (one cannot always know what rationality requires), translated as: KnowledgeOS cannot assume Determination is always accessible/transparent to the system itself.

- [S2530] types=[ARGUMENT, CORRECTION] scope=THEORY-LEVEL — "Uses non-luminosity to dissolve philosophical scepticism (if evidence were luminous, evidence would be identical between ordinary and sceptical cases, but mental states are non-luminous so the argument fails) and explicitly rejects the phenomenal conception of evidence (a converging-to-the-empty-set sequence of ever-more-private appearances), translated as: KnowledgeOS's evidence must not be modeled as private/phenomenal appearances."
